Height is determined 70% by genetics and 30% by environmental factors like nutrition, health, and exercise. There are many other variables, so the science of height prediction is not 100% accurate. Tracking your child's height with this app can show you if your child is developing normally. 

• Mid-parent Method
This method can be used if your child is less than 4 years old. Derived from a 1948 article by Horace Gray in the journal of Child Development, it is still widely used today. The margin of error is +/- 4 inches or 10.16 cm. This is a simple formula where the adult the adult height is calculated from the parents' height and the child's gender.

• Khamis-Roche Method
This method can be used for children 4 to 17 years old. Developed by Dr. Khamis and Dr. Roche, this method is around 90% accurate. It uses the child's age, gender, height, weight, parents' height along with some scaling factors and equations to predict the child's adult height.

• Bone-Age Method

The process of collecting blood from patients or blood donors is known as phlebotomy. A phlebotomist is a medical professional who performs these processes. Phlebotomists play critical roles in hospitals, clinics, testing labs, and blood donation centers. They help physicians correctly detect diseases by providing blood samples from patients. Other phlebotomist roles and responsibilities include:
Explaining to the patient why blood is being drawn 
Determining a patient's tolerance for venipuncture, or the procedure of puncturing a vein to withdraw blood
Assisting individuals in becoming comfortable throughout the procedure
Basic vitals such as blood sugar and blood pressure readings
Keeping medical supplies and equipment under their control

Phlebotomists must have a high school diploma or equivalent and complete a phlebotomy training program course, which can take four months to a year. Allied medical practitioners, such as nurses and certified nursing assistants, can also obtain phlebotomy certification to expand their skill set.

Before practice, certain states need a trained phlebotomist to be certified. Regardless of where you wish to work, a certification in the profession helps you establish yourself as a quality candidate and can help you gain a job or a higher income.
